prompt:
PLAN 11B | RUNNING AWAY FROM THE CAMERA
DURATION 15 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9
ONE CONTINUOUS HANDHELD SHOT

CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_YOUNGER_ESCAPE}}

LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_ESCAPE_EXTERIOR}}

PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_ESCAPE_ROBE}}

Create one continuous 15-second horizontal 16:9 cinematic shot following the fleeing Younger Brother FROM BEHIND.

Preserve his exact referenced identity, body proportions, handmade mask, original clothes and escape covering. The covering remains secured in its established reference arrangement, moving with his running body.

His mask stays physically fixed to his head, including during the backward glances.

LOCATION AND LIGHT

An open, uneven plain beyond the palace complex, before sunrise.

Cold blue-gray skylight reveals the ground, the runner’s silhouette and the heavy moving fabric. The mountains lie ahead of him in the distance.

The city and palace are behind the camera, outside the forward-facing composition.

Maintain soft natural predawn illumination, restrained exposure and tactile ground detail.

START STATE AND CAMERA GEOMETRY

The Younger Brother is already running forward toward the mountains.

The camera is directly BEHIND him, approximately four to five meters away, facing in the SAME direction as his travel.

His BACK faces the camera.

Use a 28mm lens at approximately the runner’s lower-chest height.

Maintain a FULL SHOT: his entire body, from the top of his head to both feet, stays within the composition, with visible ground beneath his shoes.

His figure remains prominent, occupying roughly two-thirds of the image height. The surrounding landscape provides escape space while his whole-body effort remains readable.

The operator runs forward behind him, maintaining the rear position throughout.

SHOT 11B-01 | 00s to 15s | 15 seconds

00–04s:
Follow directly behind as he runs across the uneven ground.

His stride is irregular and heavy. The covering swings behind his calves, pulls across his back and briefly catches against one leg before his next step frees it.

Camera movement carries the operator’s running footfalls: vertical bounce, slight lateral sway and small corrections to keep both feet inside the frame.

04–07s:
Without stopping, he turns his HEAD over his RIGHT shoulder to check the route behind him.

His upper torso twists only slightly; his hips and feet continue moving toward the mountains.

From the rear camera position, briefly reveal the side edge of his mask and the visible eye opening as his gaze searches past the camera toward the unseen city.

The camera remains behind him. His frightened backward glance makes his next two steps less coordinated.

He turns his head forward again.

07–11s:
He accelerates for a few strained steps, then loses strength.

One foot catches on the uneven ground. He stumbles forward, throws one arm outward to recover his balance and keeps running.

The camera lurches sideways in response, momentarily placing him off-center, then catches up and restores the full-body framing.

His bowed shoulders and shaking upper back convey crying even while his face is turned away.

11–13s:
He makes a second, shorter glance over the SAME right shoulder.

His body continues forward. His right hand grips the covering at his chest, keeping it from slipping as he checks behind.

Hold enough rear three-quarter detail to read the turn while retaining his entire body in frame.

13–15s:
He snaps his attention forward and forces himself onward.

The camera follows at the same rear distance, with the mountains still ahead and the empty route stretching around him.

End mid-stride, his back toward the lens, the covering moving heavily behind him.

CAMERA AND PERFORMANCE

Maintain rear full-body coverage throughout.

The operator follows along a real running path, matching the runner’s speed. Small distance changes are natural, but retain head-to-feet framing.

Use responsive handheld movement and brief focus corrections after the stumble. Keep his feet, backward glances and struggle with the covering legible.

His fear appears in repeated checking, disrupted balance and the effort to continue despite exhaustion.

END STATE AND EDIT

The Younger Brother continues away from the camera toward the mountains.

His head has returned forward after the final backward glance.

This is rear editorial coverage of the same escape situation. Preserve the established costume, covering and predawn conditions when intercutting with frontal coverage.

SOUND

Uneven running footsteps.
Breathing and nonverbal sobs heard from behind.
Heavy fabric snapping and dragging against clothing.
A brief shoe scrape during the stumble.
Open-air wind across the plain.

NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.
